name: webcad
description: Design mechanical parts in WebCAD, check that they build, see them and get STEP files.

interface.longDescription:
WebCAD is a CAD app that runs in the browser. With WebCAD connected, your assistant can design mechanical parts and simple mechanisms for you in WebCAD: it writes the model in ArchScript, WebCAD's text modelling language, builds it in WebCAD, shows you pictures of it, and gives you a STEP file that opens in other CAD tools or can go to a machine shop or a 3D-print service.

What you can ask for:
- Plates, brackets, enclosures, pulleys and other machined or printed parts, with holes, slots, pockets and rounded edges.
- Assemblies with joints that move, such as hinges, arms and linkages. WebCAD reports parts that collide or come apart as a joint moves through its range.
- Gear pairs and simple drivetrains.
- A first stress check of a part: a material, a fixed face and a load, with the peak stress and how far the part bends.

What you get:
- Every build reports PASS, or FAIL with the problems found, so the assistant can fix them before it calls a part done.
- Pictures of the model from the directions you ask for.
- A STEP file, made only when the build passes. Download links work for 24 hours.
- In assistants that show apps in the conversation, a 3D view of the part that you can turn and zoom, with a STEP button.

Limits:
- A PASS means the model builds in WebCAD. Whether a part is right for its purpose (fit, strength, safety, manufacturability) still needs a person's review.
- Stress results are a first check for a person to review, not an engineering sign-off.
- A build takes from about 15 seconds to a few minutes.

You need a WebCAD account (app.webcad.ca). WebCAD does not keep your scripts after a build; STEP files are deleted after 7 days, and the 3D view's part shapes after 24 hours.
capabilities: Design parts and assemblies in WebCAD
defaultPrompt: Design a 100 x 60 x 6 mm mounting plate with four M5 holes 8 mm from the edges and give me a STEP file.
Make a two-link arm with two hinge joints and show me pictures of it from the front and the side.
Design an aluminium wall bracket and check the stress when 200 N hangs from its tip.

positive.description: Design a plate with holes and deliver a STEP file
positive.prompt: Design a 100 x 60 x 6 mm mounting plate with four 5.5 mm holes 8 mm from the edges and give me a STEP file.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant writes the plate, the build passes, and export_step returns a STEP download link. The file opens in any CAD tool as one solid plate with four through holes.

positive.description: Build a two-link arm whose joints move through their range
positive.prompt: Make a two-link arm on a base with a shoulder joint and an elbow joint that each swing 90 degrees, and check that it moves without parts colliding.
positive.expected_behavior: execute_archscript returns PASS with two joints listed and each one moved through its range; if a first try collides, the assistant reads the reported problem and fixes the design before it says the arm works.

positive.description: Show rendered views of a bracket
positive.prompt: Design an L-shaped bracket with two mounting holes on each flange and show me pictures of it from the front, the top and at an angle.
positive.expected_behavior: viewport_capture returns three PNG pictures of the bracket from the requested directions, with the build result.

positive.prompt: Design a pair of spur gears, 20 and 40 teeth, module 2, on two shafts at the right centre distance, and check that it builds.
positive.expected_behavior: The build passes and lists both gears; the shafts are 60 mm apart (module 2 x (20 + 40) / 2).

positive.description: Run a first stress check on a bracket
positive.prompt: Design an aluminium wall bracket fixed at its back plate and check the stress when 200 N pulls down on its tip.
positive.expected_behavior: The build passes and the reply reports the study result (peak stress and largest displacement), and the assistant says it is a first check for a person to review.

negative.description: A general engineering question: there is no part to design, so WebCAD should not be used
negative.prompt: What is the difference between von Mises stress and maximum principal stress, and when should I use each one?
negative.expected_behavior: WebCAD is not called. The assistant answers from its own knowledge; nothing needs to be built, pictured or exported.

negative.description: A graphic design request: WebCAD makes 3D mechanical parts, not logos or images
negative.prompt: Design a logo for my machine shop, Precision Parts, in blue and silver.
negative.expected_behavior: WebCAD is not called. A logo is 2D graphic design, not a mechanical part; the assistant uses its own image tools or answers directly.

negative.description: A request for code that computes stress: the user wants a program, not a part
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that computes the bending stress in a rectangular cantilever beam with a load at its tip.
negative.expected_behavior: WebCAD is not called. The assistant writes the Python function itself; no part is built.

review.commerce_description: WebCAD does not sell anything in ChatGPT or Codex. Looking things up, checking a script, building and pictures use no credits. A STEP file uses 1 WebCAD credit, and each stress or thermal study a build runs uses 2, from the signed-in person's WebCAD account: the same credits as in the WebCAD app. Each result says what it used and what is left. Credits are managed in the WebCAD app, outside ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Exporting STEP files and running stress or thermal studies now use credits from the signed-in WebCAD account; each result says what it used. Looking things up, checking, building and pictures stay free.
